messages.author: f76413c32828a961
messages.subject: scale_x_date question
parts:
Hi there,

I am constructing a time series plot as follows:

start <- seq(as.Date("1994/1/1"), as.Date("2007/7/1"),
by="6 months")
end <- seq(as.Date("1994/7/1"), as.Date("2008/1/1"),
by="6 months")
period <- gl(2,1,length(start),
labels=c("Flu Season","Post Flu Season"))
yallp <- data.frame(start,end,period)

ytsp <- data.frame(adm=rep(seq(1000,4000,by=1000),each=7),
fdate=seq(as.Date("1994/4/1"),
as.Date("2007/10/1"), by="6 months"))

qplot(fdate,adm,geom="line",data=ytsp,xlab="Flu Season",ylab="# of
Admissions") +
geom_rect(aes(NULL,NULL,xmin=start,xmax=end,fill=period),data=yallp,
ymin=min(ytsp$adm),ymax=max(ytsp$adm)) +
scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0),major="2 years") +
scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) +
scale_fill_manual(values=alpha(c("red","blue"),0.3)) +
opts(title="Number of Hospital Admissions")

As you can see my x-axis represents flu season which I am trying to
label as 1994/1995 instead of 1994, 1995/1996 instead of 1995 and so
forth. Is there anyway to relabel the ticks? I've tried breaks and
labels similar in scale_x_continuous but keep getting error message.

Any help is much appreciated! Thank you.

Kel

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_date question
parts:
Hi Kel,

That level of control isn't currently possible with scale_x_date. The
easiest work around is to convert your dates to numbers with
as.numeric and then use scale_x_continuous.

Hadley
